MINUTES
  MALIBU CITY COUNCIL
  REGULAR MEETING
  JUNE 26, 2023
  COUNCIL CHAMBERS
  5:00 P.M.

The following meeting was held pursuant to AB 361 and teleconferenced from various
locations during the coronavirus disease (COVID-19) pandemic.

MEETING CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 5:00 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

PUBLIC COMMENT ON CLOSED SESSION

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: None.

RECESS TO CLOSED SESSION

  At 5:01 p.m., the Council recessed to Closed Session to discuss the following items listed
  on the Closed Session agenda:

Conference with Legal Counsel — Existing litigation pursuant to Government Code Section
54956.9(d)(1):

  I.  Case Name: City’s Petition to Form Malibu USD from Territory in the Santa
  Monica-Malibu USD

Conference with Legal Counsel — Anticipated Litigation

  1.  SignifiCant exposure to litigation pursuant to Government Code section
  54956.9(d)(2)
  Development Agreement between the City of Malibu and La Paz Ranch, LLC,
  regarding the property located at 23465 Civic Center Way
  Number of potential cases: (1)

  2.  Initiation of litigation pursuant to paragraph (4) of subdivision (d) of Government
  Code section 54956.9
  Number of potential cases: (1)

Personnel Matters pursuant to Government Code Section 54957:

  Public Employee Performance Evaluation
  Title; City Manager

REGULAR SESSION CALL TO ORDER

  Mayor Silverstein called the meeting to order at 6:39 p.m.

ROLL CALL

  The following persons were recorded in attendance by the Recording Secretary:

  PRESENT: Mayor Bruce Silverstein; Mayor Pro Tem Steve Uhring; and Councilmembers
  Paul Grisanti, Marianne Riggins, and Doug Stewart

  ALSO PRESENT: Trevor Rusin, Interim City Attomey; Steve McClary, City Manager;
  Joseph Toney, Assistant City Manager; Kelsey Pettijohn, City Clerk; Yolanda Bundy,
  Environmental Sustainability Director; Richard Mollica, Planning Director; Susan Duefias,
  Public Safety Director; Rob DuBoux, Public Works Director; Jason Lawrence, Deputy City
  Clerk; and Tracey Rossine, Environmental Programs Manager

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring led the Pledge of Allegiance.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

  Interim City Attomey Rusin reported that the meeting convened at 5:00 p.m., after which
  time the City Council recessed to a Closed Session pursuant to Government Code Sections
  54956.9(d)(1), 54956.9(d)(2), and 54957 with all Councilmembers present. He stated there
  was no reportable action.

REPORT ON POSTING OF AGENDA

  City Clerk Pettijohn reported that the agenda for the meeting was properly posted on June
  12, 2023, with the amended agenda posted on June 22, 2023.

APPROVAL OF AGENDA

MOTION  Councilmember Stewart moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a motion
  to approve the agenda. The question was called, and the motion carried
  unanimously.

ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  None.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Jo Drummond discussed the antennae tower at Santa Monica COllege (SMC) and
  requested the tower be reviewed by the City Council or Public Works Commission.
  She inquired when the County was notified by City staff that it was not in
  compliance. She discussed delays in permitting her deck project and stated that she
  did not understand why it took so long to permit such a small project.

  Carl Randall, Chair of the Malibu Facility District Advisory Committee (FDAC),
  stated that they were tasked with building the new high school and designing the
  four-phase project for the entire high school and middle school area. He expressed
  his concern about the impact that the California Coastal Commission’s (CCC)
  consideration of a one-year extension would have on the project, and stated the
  delay would cost $13,000,000. He stated that the August 2024 opening of the high
  school was delayed until August 2025, and it was expected to be delayed even
  further. He requested that the Council do anything they could to help, because it
  was ultimately their Local Coastal Program Amendment (LCPA) as well.

  In response to Mayor Pro Tem Uhring, Mr. Randall stated that the FDAC was
  seemingly intentionally excluded from conversations with the CCC who was
  working directly with the City.

  Stacy Rouse, Malibu FDAC member, discussed the potential delay to the Malibu
  High School (MHS) LCPA and requested intervention from the Council on behalf
  of the project. She stated that the cost to the taxpayers was astounding, and it was
  supported by 70 percent of those who voted, so it was something that the City
  wanted. She stated that the school district, local schools, and the City worked
  together to get public input on the important project and that it would serve the
  community. She stated that she wanted governmental agencies to work together for
  the good of their citizens. She stated that she would do whatever she could to
  support them in that effort and asked the Council to show their support.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Ms. Rouse stated that the bond that passed in
  2018 was for $195,000,000, which was a large portion of funds going to the first
  two phases of the project.

  Mayor Silverstein inquired if the $195,000,000 was earning some type of return
  that would help offset some of the loss from the delays.

  In response to Mayor Silverstein, Mr. Randall stated the bond funds would not be
  pulled until they were further into the project and the $13,000,000 figure was the
  loss estimated by their experts and staff from cost escalations and delays.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, Mr. Randall stated the high school
  construction project would cost approximately $110,000,000, and $115,000,000
  was the hard cost.
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023
  Page 4 of 16

Stan Smith discussed challenges he encountered during the process of trying to
rebuild like for like within the legal previously built footprint home that was lost in
the Woolsey Fire. He stated that he appreciated the previously granted extensions
and requested the Council approve an additional extension ofthe Woolsey Fire fee
waiver program. He discussed delays to his family’s settlement with Southern
California Edison and insurance challenges. He discussed his family’s ties to the
community and their desire to remain in Malibu.

Lonnie Gordon discussed wireless communications facilities in Malibu and the
telecommunications companies’ promise of wireless coverage everywhere. She
discussed the City’s Wireless ordinances and the difference between right-of-way
and private property regulations. She discussed potential health risks and effects of
exposure to radio frequencies and wireless radiation. She stated that the Malibu for
Safe Tech group of activists and experts worked with the City on ordinances, which
included one for facilities in the public right-of-way and a more robust ordinance
for facilities on private property. She stated that enhancements to the right-of-way
ordinance had yet to be incorporated, as the City decided to wait until the CCC
approved the 2021 residential revisions. She stated that the current staff status
report had 26 applications inside the residential areas, with more along the major
streets like Pacific Coast Highway (PCH) and that staff expected between 50 to 100
more applications immanently, many those in residential areas. She requested that
the Council place an item on the agenda for discussion.

W. Scott McCollough stated that he was a telecommunications lawyer and worked
with residents, staff, and City Council on the wireless ordinance update two years
prior. He discussed current Wireless rules as they related to residential areas. He
requested Council schedule an item to hear an update from staff on the ordinance,
direct staff to recognize residents’ rights to fully participate, and provide timely
access to documents. He stated that he was involved with residents on Carbon Mesa
Road and followed applications in the city and participated in select cases to assist
staff. He commented on the challenges of obtaining timely information from the
City. He discussed public safety issues that surrounded telecommunications
facilities.

Jenny stated that she spoke to City Council in 2020 and 2021 regarding the
seemingly unchecked build out of cell towers. She stated that tremendous work
went into the urgency ordinance and Resolution No. 21-17, yet there was a
proliferation of telecommunications facilities in neighborhoods, along PCH and
Kanan Dume Road, and at the SMC campus. She stated there was no gap in cell
coverage anymore to warrant more cell sites, and it was now about one
telecommunications company trying to outpace another. She requested that the City
Council place an item on the agenda that addressed unfinished business and stated
that the community relied on the Council for protection of the residents, children,
property values, views, health, and fire safety.

Stephanie Sunwoo discussed concerns about the proliferation Wireless
Communications Facilities (WCF) in residential areas and near schools. She stated
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023
  Page 5‘ of 16

MU  that she and her neighbors wanted to know What the City Council was doing to
  make their lives safer with the large influx of cell towers. She requested public
  records be made available to the community, particularly those that offered proof
  that staff did their utmost to ensure that cell towers were safe and protected the city
  from fire. She requested the matter be put on the agenda for a full hearing, including
  when the City planned on finishing the upgrade to the wireless ordinance.

  Ryan Embree discussed the communications tower in front of SMC which
  belonged to Los Angeles County and had no relation to activities at the college. He
  stated that it was an eyesore and nearly three times the height of what was allowed
  under the City’s approval. He stated that it was represented as 75 feet in height on
  the application to the City, and 91 feet in height on the application to the Federal
  Aviation Administration (FAA). He stated that the FAA conditioned the tower to
  have a flashing light on top and be painted colors that conflicted with the City’s
  conditions of approval. He stated that it was a safety hazard to the existing nearby
  helipad. He requested compliance or removal of the tower as it was a public safety
  hazard, nuisance, and violation of local and federal law. He requested the Council
  direct the Planning Director to hold a publicly noticed revocation hearing before
  the Planning Commission.

  Tim Pera, Mountains Recreation Conservation Authority (MRCA), provided the
  ranger report. He reported over the past weeks, rangers responded to three rescues
  with Los Angeles County Fire at Escondido Canyon Trail due to ankle injuries. He
  reported additional rangers and patrols were implemented at Escondido Trail during
  the high-traffic weekends for enhanced public safety and traffic control. He
  reported several illegal parking citations were issued. He reported that rangers
  continuously patrolled beach access areas daily and issued four citations for people
  having dogs on the beach and four citations for possession of alcohol at La Chuza
  Beach and Carbon La‘Costa.

  ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / COMMITTEE / CITY MANAGER UPDATES

  Lotte Cherin, Cultural Art Commission, reported that the Commission reviewed,
  made minor revisions, and approved its work assignments. She stated that the Poet
  Committee’s Poet Laureate candidate recommendation would be reviewed by the
  Arts Commission before seeking Council approval. She encouraged the Council to
  View the Jane Seymour art exhibit.

  City Manager McClary reported that he attended a meeting of the Las Virgenes-
  Malibu Council of Governments (COG), where they adopted their budget,
  approved a letter opposing the Los Angeles County Board of Supervisors motion
  to depopulate the jails, and received an update on efforts to update their hazard
  mitigation plan. He reported that he, Mayor Silverstein, and Councilmember
  Riggins met with CCC staff, and met new CCC Executive Director Dr. Kate
  Huckelbridge, who planned to visit and tour Malibu. He stated that they discussed
  the City’s short-term rental (STR) ordinance and the Sea View Hotel project. He
  announced that the City of Malibu would be closed on July 4, 2023 for the
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023
  Page 6 of 16

Independence Day holiday. He stated that the pesticide ban Local Coastal Program
Amendment (LCPA) policy interpretation would be discussed at the July 10, 2023
City Council meeting. He requested the Council consider directing staff to bring
forward an item on the July 10, 2023 meeting agenda to consider taking a position
on the CCC extension request for the high school and middle school project. He
discussed progress on Assembly Bill 1500, for property tax exemption for homes
damaged or destroyed in the Woolsey Fire. He stated that he appreciated the report
from the MRCA ranger, and that the City’s Public Safety staff was documenting
issues in and around the Winding Way and the Escondido Falls trailhead and noted
more than 400 parking citations over the past few months, and at least seven rescues
on the trail since the beginning ofthe year. He stated that City staffwould schedule
a meeting with MRCA staff to discuss issues and needed safety improvements. He
stated that staff would meet with the Los Angeles County Sheriff Department and
the Department ofBeaches and Harbors to discuss Zuma Beach traffic management
for the holiday weekend and thereafter. He stated that the Busch Drive entrance
was closed due to stream water flowing through the underpass and stated that the
Westward Beach entrance might still be closed during the upcoming weekend due
to issues with the concrete path. He stated that there were concems about traffic
backing up onto PCH, and that they would strategize with the Department of
Beaches and Harbors and the Sheriff Department to mitigate potential hazards. He
announced that all required Planning Department applications for Woolsey Fire
rebuild fee waiver projects needed to be deemed complete by the June 30, 2023
deadline, and all required building permits needed to be pulled and issued by
December 30, 2023. He stated that there were no firework permits or planned
displays off of the coast this year for the July 4, 2023 Independence Day holiday.

Sergeant Chris Soderlund, Los Angeles County Sheriff Department, provided an
update on activities by the special assignment deputies over the past two weeks. He
reported the aftemoon deputies made five misdemeanor arrests and conducted
numerous traffic stops. He stated that on June 16, 2023, during a vehicle burglary
investigation, they arrested an individual in possession of stolen property and
narcotics. He reported that the overnight special assignment deputies made two
misdemeanor arrests, assisted regular patrol units with calls, and made a felony
arrest of an individual who they contacted about a shopping cart violation on June
22, 2023 during a foot patrol at Legacy Park. He stated that the individual had two
outstanding no-bail warrants for narcotics, and one misdemeanor warrant. He
reported that on June l9, 2023, in response to an individual trespassing in yards at
31 100 Broad Beach Road, the Sheriff helicopter with multiple deputies contained
the area and the suspect was found hiding between rocks on the beach. He stated
that deputies found that he had broken into two houses, he was arrested and charged
with burglary, and was still in jail. He provided beach team statistics for the prior
weekend and reported 55 alcohol on the beach citations, 64 traffic citations, and
132 parking citations were issued, and 18 vehicles were towed. He stated that the
Sheriff Department would be out in full force over the Independence Day holiday
weekend. He reported that deputies responded the prior Saturday to a domestic
violence in progress incident at Geoffrey’s restaurant. He stated that the suspect
was arrested for suspicion of domestic violence and for possession of a loaded 45
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023
  Page 7 of 16

  caliber semiautomatic pistol which was found in the vehicle.

  In response to Councilmember Stewart, Sergeant Sutherland discussed the
  temporary day-use impound yard at Malibu High School and stated that it was
  invaluable for clearing vehicles off PCH, traffic flow, and accident prevention.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring commented on noise from PCH and encouraged the Sheriff
  Department to do what they could to reduce noise.

  Councilmember Grisanti commented on minibikes without license plates and some
  riders without helmets that the Sheriff Department turned back and escorted north
  out of Malibu.

ITEM 2.C.  SUBCOMMITTEE REPORTS / COUNCIL COMMENTS

  Councilmember Grisanti stated he attended a Topanga Watershed proj ect meeting
  two weekends prior and met with State Parks staff and discussed low-cost Visitor
  serving accommodation projects that could be eligible for funding in the future. He
  reported that he attended the COG meeting. He reported that he attended the
  Sidewalk Session event with Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin and Fire Department
  Chief Drew Smith on June 24, 2023.

  Councilmember Stewart reported that he attended the Administration and Finance
  Subcommittee meeting and reviewed the budget. He reported that he viewed the
  Topanga Watershed meeting presentation and attended the COG meeting as an
  alternate. He stated that he participated with Mayor Pro Tem Uhring in a virtual
  presentation with local school leaders regarding fund raising efforts in support of
  school athletic programs. He discussed the one-year delay in building MHS and
  stated that since the bond was approved November 8, 201 8 the cost of construction
  increased 30 percent, and plans may need to be pared back or more funds raised.
  He stated that public and private projects were impacted by delays due to increased
  costs and inflation. He stated that the City was constrained by federal law regarding
  wireless communication facilities (WCF), but public records needed to be made
  available to those concerned who requested access to the documents. He discussed
  California Highway Patrol vehicles that were visible in the City and expressedhis
  appreciation.

  Councilmember Riggins stated that she attended Assemblymember Irwin’s
  greeting event and it was good to discuss issues with her. She stated she attended
  the Malibu Creek Restoration meeting and discussed potential impacts the planned
  removal of the Rindge Dam would have on Malibu. She stated that she attended the
  local school education funding proposal presentation.

  Mayor Pro Tem Uhring reported that he attended the weekly Califomia Strategies
  meetings. He stated that he attended the Malibu Creek Restoration meeting and was
  impressed by the team and their proposal. He stated that he spoke with Steve
  Massetti about CCC delays to the MHS project. He discussed the State Assembly
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023
  Page 8 of 16

Bill which would allow speed cameras as a pilot program and stated that he hoped
Malibu would be included in the program in the future. He discussed a letter he
received about the farmers’ market and stated he thought they were doing a good
  'at
job and he hoped it would remain  Legacy Park. He discussed the negative
impacts of corporate-owned STRs on communities and neighborhoods. He
discussed the Planning Commission’s election of Chair and Vice Chair at the June
19, 2023 Planning Commission meeting and commented on Commissioner
Mazza’s volunteerism and contributions to the City.

Mayor Silverstein stated he attended an Administration and Finance Subcommittee
meeting and a meeting on public school funding. He stated that he attended
California Strategies virtual meetings and a virtual meeting with CCC staff to
discuss STRs. He discussed concerns that public documents were not made
available and voiced his confidence that staff would not intentionally hide
documents but was concerned information was not readily available due to
organizational or staffing issues.

In response to Mayor Silverstein, City Manager McClary stated that the documents
in questio‘n might have been draft applications that were a work product and not
considered a public record but assured him that anything that was public record
request would be complied with.

In response to Mayor Silverstein, Interim City Attorney Rusin stated that the
materials in question may have been copywritten materials produced for in-person
review. He stated that until such materials were presented at a Planning
Commission meeting, or an approval issued, the copywrite applied and they would
not be able to be reproduced or mailed to requesting parties.
  w

Mayor Silverstein requested specific information on the documents that requesting
parties felt were denied but were legally entitled to. He stated that a few months
prior he requested an item be placed on an agenda about conforming the wireless
right-of-way ordinance to the non-right-of-way ordinance. He stated the right-of-
way ordinance was adopted on an accelerated basis, and they then did the non-right-
of-way ordinance and looked at it more carefully, and the first one needed to be
made consistent with it. He stated that it had made more sense to wait until the CCC
approved the ordinance before the City started making changes, but if that was not
going to happen soon, they should proceed with bringing it forward without the
CCC review.

In response to Mayor Silverstein, Planning Director Mollica discussed the WCF
LCPA extension through November 2023. He stated that the CCC passed a one-
year extension in November 2022, and he spoke against it and that the City
understood that CCC staff was burdened and offered to help them to get it on track,
but the extension was approved. He stated that staff had requested feedback, but
none was provided, and stated that he would follow up with them.

Mayor Silverstein thanked him, and stated November 2023 was coming up a lot
   Malibu City Council
  Minutes of June 26, 2023

  sooner than when he flrst spoke about the matter many months ago.

CONSENSUS
  By consensus, the Council directed staff to bring back an item at the August 14,
  2023 Regular meeting to receive-a report from staff and consider giving direction
  on modifying the Wireless Communication Facility right-of-way ordinance.

  In response to public comment, Mayor Silverstein indicated support for proving
  additional relief for residents eligible for a Woolsey Fire Rebuild fee waiver and
  stated that litigation with SCE lasted much longer than anyone anticipated and
  . moved slowly. He suggested staff develop a limited further waiver for certain
  residents who wished to rebuild like-for—like.

  Item Nos. 3.B.5., 3.B.7., 3.B.12., and 3.B.16. were pulled by the public. Item No.

  Commission Work Assignments for Fiscal Year 2023-24
  Recommended Action: Approve work assignments for the Harry Barovsky
  Memorial Youth Commission, Malibu Arts Commission, Parks and
  Recreation Commission, Public Safety Commission and Public Works
  Commission for Fiscal Year 2023-24.

  Mayor Silverstein opened the floor to public comment.

  Speakers: Jo Drummond and Ryan Embree

  As there were no other speakers present, Mayor Silverstein returned the
  matter to the table for discussion.

  The Council discussed the item and directed questions to staff.

MOTION  Councilmember Riggins moved, and Councilmember Grisanti seconded a
  motion to approve work assignments for the Harry Barovsky Memorial
  Youth Commission, Malibu Arts Commission, Parks and Recreation
  Commission (as amended to add an assignment to consider potential uses
  for the Equestrian Park), Public Safety Commission, and Public Works
